newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday June 6.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said his Freedom Alliance did not back the government's proposal for electoral system reform. Ruling coalition favours a two-round electoral system in order to increase the parliamentary power and to make a semi-presidential system more balanced (all).
* Hard left Communist Refoundation party called on the government to fight a recommendation that the country should adopt a presidential-style electoral system (all).

* Government heralded a preliminary agreement between banking association ABI and unions over job cuts and restructuring in the banking sector. The accord was praised by Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio, while cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said labour costs at Italian banks were some 30 percent higher than the European average and the sector needed to shed between 30-45,000 million jobs (all).
* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed retail sales of medium and large firms in Italy rose 1.3 percent in February 1997 compared with a year earlier (Sole 24 Ore).
* State engineering company Finmeccanica named Sergio Carbone as chairman and Alberto Lina as vice chairman and chief executive officer (all).
* Agip's parent ENI said state-run China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) and Agip Spa have signed an agreement to form a joint oil venture (Sole 24 Ore).
* Banking group Banco Ambroveneto said it would outsource all its data processing activity to Daimler-Benz unit Debis Systemhaus in a 10-year deal worth one trillion lire (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
